title: Testing finite Tor amplitude at the residue field
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $n\geq1$, put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and $\kappa=A/(\varpi_E)$, and let $T$ be a scheme. Write $A_T,\kappa_T$ for the constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on the small etale site of $T$. Let $K\in D(T_{\Et},A)$ in the ordinary derived category [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] have bounded constructible cohomology [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. For integers $a,b$, $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude] if and only if
$$
\mathcal H^i(K\otimes_A^L\kappa_T)=0\qquad(i\notin[a,b]),
$$
where derived tensor is the etale construction [def-kun-derived-tensor].

proof.text: Let r be the image of the chosen uniformizer in A. Its nth power is zero by the defining level-n quotient. From [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], the principal uniformizer ideal in the integer ring is maximal. Since n>=1 its nth power is contained in itself, so its image in A is maximal. Ideal.map_span identifies this image with (r). These are the coefficient facts needed by the categorical criterion; no separate finiteness or locality result is used.

Apply [lem-exc-categorical-nilpotent-residue-test] to C=Sheaf(T_Et,ModuleCat A), R=A and the scalar r. The existing etale tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor] is definitionally this derived monoidal tensor. The quotient residue sheaf is the required cokernel by [lem-exc-constant-quotient-sheaf-cokernel], and [lem-exc-residue-sheaf-tensor-monomorphism] supplies preservation of monomorphisms, using the maximality proved in step 1. The categorical criterion implements exactly the K-flat killed-by-r argument followed by induction on the nilpotent scalar filtration; no comparison with a pro-etale site is made.

For the forward implication evaluate [def-kun-tor-amplitude] at the constant residue module. Conversely, split the explicit vanishing hypothesis into vanishing below a and above b, then apply DerivedCategory.isGE_iff and isLE_iff to obtain the two standard t-structure bounds. The criterion of step 2 gives those bounds after tensoring with every test sheaf M in degree zero. Convert them back with the same two equivalences and split i<a or b<i. This is exactly the universal vanishing predicate [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. No a<=b hypothesis is used, and bounded constructibility is retained without being needed.

proof_origin.place: Existing categorical nilpotent-scalar criterion, with generic site inputs from lean/WeilConjectures/SixFunctors/ProEtale/FiniteCoefficient/Derived/TorAmplitudeResidue.lean; applied on the small etale site and combined with explicit coefficient-ideal calculations and t-structure/vanishing equivalences by X9, 2026-10-18. This is the same filtration argument as the previous node proof.

Steps 1-3, 5 and 6 are correct: A_T/ϖA_T≅κ_T by exact sheafification (00WJ); the K-flat resolution is Stacks 06YS; the ϖ-adic filtration F_n=0 is finite with quotients killed by ϖ; flatness of each P^q gives degreewise short exact sequences, and the long exact sequence (0117) gives the descending induction. Boundedness, constructibility and finite generation of M are never used. Small cases on a geometric point over Z/4 agree with the criterion: A[0], Z/2[0] (infinite Tor dimension), and [A→2 A]; n=1, a>b and empty T are also covered. There is no cycle and no SGA source. This claim has its own hypotheses, its proof is repeated word for word in lem-sf-proetale-residue-tor-test, and the blueprint lem-weil-field-tor-amplitude uses it without proof.
